newsitem.title: INDIA: India Haldia Petrochemicals sees output from 1999.
newsitem.headline: India Haldia Petrochemicals sees output from 1999.

text.p: Haldia Petrochemicals Limited (HPL), a venture involving India's Tata group, Japan's Toyo group and international investor George Soros, said on Friday its petrochemical unit will start output in 1999.

"Toyo Engineering Corporation of Japan has started the construction of the naptha cracker plant at Haldia from Thursday and commercial production in the naptha cracker and other plants would start within 30 months," company chairman Anish Majumdar told reporters in Calcutta.
The 51.7 billion rupee ($1.4 billion) project is being built at Haldia, a port town in the eastern state of West Bengal, of which Calcutta is the capital.
The state-run West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) holds 51 percent in the firm in which the U.S.-based Chatterjee Soros group and the Tatas are partners.
The Chatterjee Soros group joined after India invited foreign investors under an economic reform programme launched in 1991.
Company officials said the WBIDC, had already put in 5.0 billion rupees of its contribution to the equity and an equal amount would be put in shortly.
"All the down payments and financial guarantees required for the construction contract have been effected," Majumdar said at a news conference held after a board meeting in Calcutta.

Tata group chairman Ratan Tata described the beginning of project construction at Haldia as " major milestone" in industrial rejuvenation of eastern India, believed to have suffered on account of socialist controls and labour disputes.
"We are proud that we have stake in the project. We will support the project all through," Tata said.
Purnendu Chatterjee, an expatriate Indian who formed the Chatterjee Soros group, said the debt-equity ratio of the project was 1.6:1.
"Of the total project cost 20 billion rupees is equity, while the debt component is 31.7 billion," Chatterjee said.
"There need not be any scepticism now about the implementation of the project," said Chatterjee, who is also the vice-chairman of HPL. ($1=35.8 rupees)
